diagnosis: Candidate/bad runs overrepeat UI/tool actions without gaining new progress, especially clicks, no-ops, and scrolls.
expected_mechanism: A progress gate detects action loops and forces diagnosis or a materially different strategy. This should reduce wasted operations and timeout exposure, at the cost of small bookkeeping overhead and occasional premature strategy changes.
policy_text: Before repeating an action, compare the current state and result with the previous attempt. If no material progress occurred, do not repeat unchanged: diagnose the blocker, alter the action or strategy, or stop and report the limitation. Track repeated attempts per objective and impose a small retry limit.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r '[.value, (if (.stack_frames[] == "result:repeated") then 1 else 0 end)] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{if($1>0){allp+=$1;if($2)rp+=$1}else{alln+=-$1;if($2)rn+=-$1}} END{printf "candidate repeated=%d/%d (%.2f%%); base repeated=%d/%d (%.2f%%); rate_ratio=%.2fx\n",rp,allp,100*rp/allp,rn,alln,100*rn/alln,(rp/allp)/(rn/alln)}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated operations were 1,485/7,366 (20.16%) on the candidate/bad side versus 224/3,780 (5.93%) on the base/good side: a 3.40× rate ratio and +1,261 net excess.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[] == "result:repeated") | [.value, (.stack_frames[] | select(startswith("action:")))] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{s[$2]+=$1} END{for(k in s) print s[k],k}' | sort -nr
quantitative_evidence.finding: The repeated-operation excess was concentrated in action:click (+639), action:noop (+356), and action:scroll (+277), demonstrating a recurring interaction loop rather than a single isolated action.

quantitative_evidence.command: jq -r 'select(.stack_frames[] == "result:repeated") | [.value, (.stack_frames[] | select(startswith("task:")))] | @tsv' samples.jsonl | awk -F '\t' '{s[$2]+=$1; if($1>0)p[$2]=1; else n[$2]=1} END{for(k in s){if(s[k]>0)netpos++; if(p[k])pt++; if(n[k])nt++} print "candidate_tasks="pt,"base_tasks="nt,"net_positive_tasks="netpos}'
quantitative_evidence.finding: Repeated behavior appeared in 64 candidate-side tasks versus 18 base-side tasks, with positive net excess in 59 tasks, confirming recurrence across tasks.
